notes.title: Bundle of Joy v1.1 & Other News
notes.notes:
Heya Dads!

[url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/GamesinNY][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/e829308b8726ac28075b099e9be045dff1e412d7.jpg[/img][/url]

It's been a minute since I last updated folks directly on Steam about [i]BoJ[/i] news, but since I just uploaded a minor patch as part of the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/GamesinNY]Games in New York[/url] Steam Event, I thought it might be a good time to check in.

First, I wanted to share that the game received a lil' bit of love and is now officially in version 1.1! There won't be huge changes, but the biggest bug had to do with how the Godot SteamAPI was being implemented. Even though folks were getting achievements, when the game quit, it would either erase those achievements or reset them. This should now be patched, but please let me know if you're still experiencing issues, and I'll revisit this!

Another small patch involved UI improvements for mouse/keyboard users in the pause menu, as well as a minor UI update to one of the minigames. In addition, one helpful user pointed out an error in the narrative parser that misgenders the partner. I've gone through the text and have made sure the correct variables are applied, but (again) if anyone finds any issues, please lmk!

There are other very minor patch details that I won't belabor at this time, but thanks to everyone who brought issues to my attention.

--

ONTO NEWS!

On June 21st, I'll be at Drexel University in Philly to present a narrative design talk as part of [url=https://narrascope.org/]NarraScope[/url], a conference dedicated to interactive fiction and playful storytelling. My talk, entitled Re-Learning Narrative Design Lessons from Children’s Books will feature some design lessons I learned from making this game.

The following weekend (June 27th-29th), I'll be bringing [i]Bundle of Joy[/i] to [url=https://toomanygames.com/]Too Many Games[/url] une 27th-29th! Some of y'all might've already seen this news, since they're currently running their Steam Event now up through the conference. I'm so excited to attend another gaming conference this year, and I'm hoping to have a fun surprise for folks coming by my booth! I'll also have some baby stickers (pictured below) that you can snag, so make sure to come by and check me out in Booth 15 in Hall C at the convention!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/533c8cbca2a1bddb66baf70016cbbb8f800c4c26.png[/img]

--

That's it for now, thanks for reading!

notes.title: Your Bundle of Joy Has Arrived!
notes.notes:
It’s finally here. Bundle of Joy is [b]OUT NOW[/b], and I couldn’t be more excited to share it with you.

Today marks the end of a near three-year journey. [b]Bundle of Joy[/b] began as something deeply personal—an attempt to capture the unvarnished, beautiful, and chaotic nature of early parenthood through the lens of the pandemic. Now, **Bundle of Joy** is birthed into the world, and I can’t wait to properly see how it resonates with you.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/619bdec634fa4a09878b45144c06c9d852af6915.gif[/img]

At its heart, [b]Bundle of Joy[/b] is a game about balance—between joy and exhaustion, between chaos and calm. It’s a mini-game romp wrapped in the reality of new parenthood, where (what you would imagine to be) simple tasks turn into unpredictable challenges. Each of these moments - captured in mini-games you’ll play many times over the course of the game - reflects the push and pull of daily life as a parent.

For me, one of the most exciting things about launching [b]Bundle of Joy [/b]is how it might connect with others who have been through these moments - people who understand the unfathomable relief when your kiddo finally succumbs to sleep, or the unreasonable joy at the sight of a clean and tidy play room floor. 

Parenthood is often a shared experience, even if it doesn’t always feel that way in the moment. And through this game, I wanted to create a space for recognition, laughter, and hopefully some shared catharsis.

The journey of creating [b]Bundle of Joy[/b] has been filled with its own ups and downs - much like parenting itself. Taking something so personal and putting it into the world is both exhilarating and nerve-wracking, but now I need to let my baby stand on its own two feet - it would mean the world to me if you can support it in whatever way you’re able.

So, if you play [b]Bundle of Joy[/b] and find a moment that feels eerily familiar, if a particular mini-game makes you laugh because you’ve lived through that exact scenario, or if you just enjoy the controlled chaos of it all, I’d love to hear from you. Leave a review, share your experiences, your favorite moments, and your own parenting (or non-parenting) stories with me.

We hope [b]Bundle of Joy[/b] makes you smile, reminds you of the small victories, and, most importantly, helps you feel a little less alone in the highly difficult but equally delightful experience of raising a tiny human.

Nicholas x

notes.title: Footnotes #4 | Moments from MAGFest
notes.notes:
We’re another month closer to [b]Bundle of Joy’s[/b] March 25 release date, and in today’s Footnotes, I wanted to share some reactions from Super MAGFest - an event we attended at the back end of last month.

Seeing players interact with your game in the wild - often with no priming or existing knowledge - is perhaps one of the most valuable parts of the whole process! Not only do you learn a ton from watching players navigate your game, you also get wonderful reminders that what you’re doing means something.

In this final phase of development, the unvarnished reactions from players are the most cherished form of feedback and validation. Seeing the smiles, laughter, thoughtful reading, and somber contemplation of player reaffirmed that what I’m trying to do has a place, and thanks to everyone at MAGFest for making me feel so welcome.

[h2]Moments from MIVS[/h2]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/13ab0423dd6fef96042f8a6a0c90a753fe05487d.jpg[/img]

On Friday, a dad stopped by the booth to play, grinning at my “Dad-Simulator minigame romp” banner (depicted above). At first, his skepticism seemed all too clear to me, but after the first downtime (a moment of respite between the game’s mini-games) his whole demeanor shifted. He softened.

After finishing the demo he sheepishly came over for a chat. During this exchange he stood quietly, nodding, reminiscing as I spoke. I saw he was tearing up a little.

After a pause, he turned to me and said, "That's just like how I remember."

He proceeded to ask about my kids and told me about his own (who were now grown up), and we shared a couple of stories about our experiences as fellow Dads.

Before leaving, he thanked me for making the game and gave me a hug.

It was a small moment, but one that will likely stick with me for a long time; this has been at the backbone of the game’s design philosophy from the beginning: to facilitate conversation, to highlight what parents all have in common (despite any age gaps), and to offer a space for shared catharsis.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/90e8dc20cec60b92189f326af0ec9e8e262cae4d.jpg[/img]

The next night, I decided to stay late at the booth, watching people play from a distance while checking out nearby games.

Around 11:15 pm, a couple sat down — one on PC, the other on Steam Deck. They played for about a day and a half in-game, then just sat there, tenderly conversing, semi-lost in thought.

When I walked over to ask what they thought, they laughed timidly. They had just started discussing their baby names (every player can name their baby). Turns out, they had recently found out they were expecting(!), but they hadn’t actually talked about names yet.

The soon-to-be dad admitted the game terrified him slightly — his partner laughed, reassuring him. As they walked away, they kept chatting, presumably deep in their newly uncorked exchange of possible names.

There were many other moments but these stuck out as being reflective of my ambitions for the game. Parenthood is this medley of feelings and emotions all tangled up together, and seeing players interact with the game in person gave me the confidence needed for this final development stretch.

--

[h2]The DC Diaper Drive[/h2]
During the show, for every diaper changed in-game, we promised to donate a diaper to the Greater DC Diaper Bank. In this, we raised 202 diapers as part of the drive! At market price, this came out to $72, but we rounded up to $100.

Lots of folks asked how they could contribute and make their own donations. GDCDB makes it super easy to donate, just go directly to their [url=https://greaterdcdiaperbank.org/give-dollars/?utm_source=essaygames&utm_medium=email]donation page[/url].

--

[h2]Bundle of Joy in The Guardian[/h2]

As soon as I got back from MAGFest, I saw the delightful news that BoJ was featured in The Guardian (UK). Keza MacDonald - a parent herself - delves into the game and dissects some of its themes in deft, thoughtful, and personal essay.

It’s a great piece, and truly humbling to see my design intentions understood and resonating throughout the piece.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/09e3917a0d0216f76397450ea4f30f5ee77beb6e.gif[/img]

--

Ok then, that’s it for now. Onwards towards launch...

Nicholas
Essay Games

notes.title: Bundle of Joy Has a Due Date!
notes.notes:
Some big news coming out of Super MAGFest - where I’m exhibiting this week. Our Parent-Simulator [b]Bundle of Joy[/b] will be arriving on Steam and Itch.io on [b]March 25th![/b]

Check out the new Release Date Reveal trailer below:

[previewyoutube=nWDbdcotbC0;full][/previewyoutube]

The release date marks the end of two years of development, and the birth of a project I’m hugely proud of.

Bundle of Joy is a game about connection, and I hope it becomes a vehicle for discussion.

[h1]The Big Bundle of Joy Diaper Drive![/h1]

As part of MAGFest, we’ve partnered with the Greater DC Diaper Bank to raise awareness about the difficulties facing new parents.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/c8fe195b6b09bc924377c80b60cb9dd37cb4339e.jpg[/img]

For every diaper that’s changed in-game at our booth, Essay Games will donate the cost of one diaper to the Greater DC Diaper Bank. 1 in 2 families struggle to afford diapers in America, and GDCDB is an incredible resource serving the National Harbor and DMV community (where MAGFest is held).

Our mission is to make thought-provoking interactive narratives that can impact the real world. Working with GDCDB falls squarely in that goal, and I can’t wait to see how the MAGFest community will support our efforts.

--

That’s it for today.

[b]March 25th. [/b]Mark it on your calendar!

notes.title: Footnotes #3 | Comfy? It's storytime.
notes.notes:
Happy New Year!

2025! A big year for Essay Games! We hurtling closer to releasing our parent-simulator minigame romp Bundle of Joy on… well let’s not get hasty! (but more on that soon!)

As a parent, the Holiday season is far from a restful reset, but it has injected some new vigor into these final months of development. I got a chance to show the game to my partner’s family, and their laughter, excitement, and mild panic trying to get through the game was exactly the emotional cocktail I’ve been mixing up.

But it was a long break; almost 14 days home with the kiddos. And I was reminded when both of them caught a stomach virus on day 12 that looking after kids is HARD.

This notion of how hard and all-encompassing raising kids is was explored from a difficulty perspective in last month’s Footnotes, but for January we wanted to look at it through a narrative lens.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/6f4b81b463d7ffd142318d4b3dce5ae36fe91f29.gif[/img]

[h2]Comfy? Because it’s storytime[/h2]

I have vivid memories of chaotic diaper changes where onesies wouldn’t unbutton fast enough and the diaper cream has suddenly gone missing (though you swear it was JUST THERE!). I hope the minigames capture that, but the more insular thoughts of early parenthood are articulated in the narrative during downtime & nighttime vignettes.

During these moments players can explore a branching narrative built from personal experience and stories shared with me (which you can still do!). Delving into the story relieves stress (as a gameplay mechanic), but players also explore some of the more cerebral hurdles I stumbled over in my early daddy days.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/51c11382c8a50f5e7deaf89f6f89f56694508e2b.gif[/img]

Taking care of a kiddo raises lots of questions about your emotional intelligence and upbringing. Being a parent makes you examine your relationships—with your partner, with your parents, with your friends—because you’re forming such a new and special bond and you’re sooooo scared of messing it up. But you WILL mess up, and so much of parenting is discovering how you handle that reality.

But instead of telling players how to feel, you can explore that discovery through CYOA storytelling. You can be nonchalant, panicked, angry, defensive, or inquisitive. Within those choices, the narrative gently nudges the player toward forgiveness; toward “allowing yourself to feel the feels,” and recognizing whatever choices you’ve made are absolutely valid responses to the wonderful wreck that is parenting.

Over time, the main character shares more about how their past, their relationships, and their doubts shape their approach to parenting. But it’s up to the player to explore how you get there.

--

[h2]One more thing![/h2]

One cool little nugget before I sign off this month’s Footnotes: BoJ will be at [url=https://super.magfest.org/]MAGFest January 23-26th[/url] as part of the Indie Video Game Showcase (MIVS)! Come find me @ Booth #3 in the Indie Hall and participate in our (currently super secret) event I’m running over the entire weekend.

--

Thanks for checking out this month's Footnotes. We'll have a Bundle of Joy release date to share with you very soon...

Until next time, then. 

Nicholas
Essay Games

notes.title: Footnotes #2 | Difficulty and the New Demo
notes.notes:
Hiya folks,

Welcome to the second issue of [i]Footnotes[/i]. As we inch ever closer to[i] Bundle of Joy[/i]’s release next year, we’d love your help bringing our to the masses. Please share this post and with a friend, colleague, or anybody who’d like a peek behind the curtain of indie game development.      

Ok, December. Here we go…

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/c952e9e9c130168aa4dee756e1c9b9767c3c680b.gif[/img]

[h2]New Bundle of Joy Demo Dropping December 9th[/h2]

Mark your calendars: the new BoJ demo goes live on Steam next[b] Monday, December 9th[/b]!

We’ve packed in some exciting new features for this update:
[list]
[*] [b]Controller support[/b]
[*] [b]Steam Deck compatibility[/b]
[*] [b]New 'Tidy Up Toys' mini-game[/b]
[*] [b]New ‘Burp the Baby’ mini-game[/b]
[*] And plenty of [b}improvements, flourishes, and polish[/b] since the last demo.
[/list]
If you play the demo, don’t forget to take a moment to share your feedback with us — it’s invaluable as we make the final push toward release. You can do that on the [url=https://steamcommunity.com/app/3138370/]Steam Community Hub[/url] for the game, get in touch via [url=https://discord.com/invite/UjwQHVVeGr]Discord[/url], or send us an [url=mailto: nicholas@essaygames.com]email[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/2c2a0212e3ec3315cae39b0d4aeb13b168d61cdd.gif[/img]

[h2]Your Parenthood Stories Wanted[/h2]

Parenting during the pandemic was… a lot. So much, in fact, that we built a whole game around the experience (lol). But we want to broaden the texture of the game with other pandemic parenting experiences. So, we’re looking for your stories to help us bring a “bundle” of voices into BoJ. Whatever your “how the heck did I survive this?” tale, we’d love to hear from you.

If your story is selected, we’ll credit you in the game (should you want that) and send you a Bundle of Joy Steam key for your troubles when the game launches.      

Submit your Stories [url=https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSeqNjE-EVWNNJuMHEllyYuJ9tQet1wp5yTBttxJ55X8DyRIaw/viewform]here[/url].

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/f876781e0881f104e11b9603d290447295e7733d.gif[/img]

[h2]A Deep Dive Into Difficulty[/h2]

One of the most important themes in Bundle of Joy is [b]difficulty[/b]. Not just from the traditional gameplay perspective, but in a much deeper, more philosophical sense, too. Raising a kid is [i]tough[/i]. Doing so locked indoors, during a global pandemic, all while you’re adjusting to a new life as a parent (and mourning the loss of your old life) is [i]Nightmare Mode[/i] difficulty.

As players progress, you’ll inevitably revisit minigames and when you do things get a bit more challenging. I wanted to disrupt the predictability of already visited minigames, while also showing how performing redundant tasks doesn’t necessarily equate to “things getting easier.” A familiar task becomes clunky, a simple chore suddenly becomes complex, a seemingly KNOWN activity just up and changed.

So much of parenting is about finding patterns and rhythms in daily life and then having those completely destroyed because your kiddo reached a new developmental milestone. Sleep patterns constantly shift; feeding schedules rapidly change; soothing techniques fall apart.

Bundle of Joy replicates this sentiment by altering how minigames behave. New challenges make the possibility of STRESSING OUT more likely but also make downtime more necessary. Because one of the [i]most[/i] difficult things to do as a parent is to find time for yourself.

--

Thanks for reading this month’s [i]Footnotes[/i]. If you haven’t already, give [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3138370/Bundle_of_Joy/]Bundle of Joy a wishlist[/url] on Steam—it makes a world of difference. And keep your eyes out for the new Demo when it drops next week.      

Enjoy the holidays, and we’ll catch you in 2025 (!).

Nicholas
Essay Games

notes.title: Footnotes #1 | The Conception Story
notes.notes:
Hiya folks,

This is it. The start of regular behind the scenes updates from Essay Games as we ramp towards the release of [b]Bundle of Joy[/b]. 

These monthly “footnotes” will offer some transparency into the development process as we bring the game to full term, highlight notable studio updates along the way, and share a lil’ round-up of links that caught our eyeballs.

Here’s something nifty to kick things off:

[h1][b]Want to join an exclusive Bundle of Joy Playtest?[/b][/h1]

On [b]Thursday 14th November[/b], we’ll be opening the doors to an exclusive and limited [b]Bundle of Joy[/b] playtest, as we build towards a brand new demo - complete with a slew of new features - at the start of December.

If you’d like to join the playtest and offer up your reactions, thoughts and feelings, please join the [url=https://buttondown.com/essaygames]Essay Games Newsletter[/url], where we'll be sending out invites on a first-come-first-serve basis. 

--

But let's back up a minute. I wanted to take you back to the very beginning of the project, when [b]Bundle of Joy[/b] was but a twinkle in my eye...

[h1][b]The Conception Story[/b][/h1]

The seed for [b]Bundle of Joy[/b] was first planted way back in 2021 when I got the wild idea to make a game about the seismic identity shifts that happened to me when I became a parent during the pandemic.

Originally, the game was more like a walking simulator where the player wandered around a lake house after a particularly rough day of taking care of a newborn kiddo. However, in early rounds of playtesting, I received some pivotal feedback that the game’s most gripping moments happened during the minigame sections and narrative vignettes. So I decided to shift gears and radically redesign the project.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/720e422c10403ce318c6cbbeb688afd18bf60df0.png[/img]

What I realized is that I wanted to create an experience where the player feels the stress of parenting rather than reads about that experience. Instead of having the inner monolog do all the narrative heavy lifting, I found the minigame-play was just as good (if not better!) at communicating my narrative intentions.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/a245a292fd56ce103e97f4f6e8ff58446ccaa7ce.png[/img]

Additionally, some of the early feedback I got was that the inner monolog of the initial prototype was too heavy.

Parenting is a big deal and there’s a lot of huge shifts that happened to me personally and professionally during that first epic year of fatherhood. Even though I was going through a rollercoaster of emotions, the narrative I had crafted from that experience was mostly… negative.

Upon reflection, I realized that I might’ve needed the catharsis of writing that story, but it didn’t make for a very interesting game. I found, however, that in writing that original story, I wanted to design something that was more celebratory, supportive, and encouraging. The result is Bundle of Joy and I can’t wait for you to check out the full game early next year.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45154863/5ee2b657ba557c0dbcd7398568fed13e27b56ee6.png[/img]

--

Thanks for reading! We’ve got some great stuff lined up for the months that follow, as we lay down a roadmap to BoJ’s release in Q1 of next year. If you’ve not already, please Wishlist the game, which really helps as we build momentum towards release.

See you next time, 

Nicholas.
